newsitem.title: KUWAIT: Kuwait paper says right to host U.S. warplanes.
newsitem.headline: Kuwait paper says right to host U.S. warplanes.

text.p: A Kuwaiti newspaper said on Friday the Gulf country's decision to allow U.S. warplanes to use its territory for possible action against Iraq was justified to guarantee Kuwait's security.
"The only language this neighbour (Iraq) understands is power, hence we are obliged to deploy all possible means to deter this regime," al-Watan newspaper said in an editorial.

Eight U.S. F-117A stealth bombers which took off from a U.S. Airforce base on Thursday were expected to land at a Kuwaiti air base on Friday evening to beef-up U.S. presence in the region for possible new action against Iraq.
Baghdad told Kuwait on Thursday it would be committing an act of war if it allowed the U.S. planes to use its territory for attacks on Iraq

"Kuwait's primary interest, undisputably, is to protect its territory, regardless of any comments expressed here or there," said the paper, apparently anticipating criticism of Kuwait's decision by some Arab states.

"We know well that we are dealing with a criminal (Iraqi President Saddam Hussein) who loves shedding blood," Watan said. "Kuwait, this small country, is doing nothing more than an attempt to protect its territory."
Iraq invaded Kuwait in 1990 and annexed it for seven months. About 300 Kuwaitis were killed and hundreds were tortured in the occupation. A U.S.-led coalition ejected Iraq in February 1991.
Prominent Kuwait columnist Fouad al-Hashem wrote in a separate opinion column in Watan on Friday: "The recent Iraqi threat to Kuwait makes us wonder until when should this nightmare continue?"

To topple Saddam it would only take "a bullet worth 20 Iraqi fils (less than one U.S. cent) fired by one of his military leaders...Those (U.S.) carriers, warplanes and missiles are like a surgeon's knife -- they make him stronger; they do not make him fall," said Hashem.
